text:
Brock Nelson tipped in a goal and left after taking a shot to the ear in the same win over Calgary on Oct. 31 (Yahoo Sports), and was back in the lineup two days later. The scoring has been slower than the toughness: four points in his last ten games, where our numbers expected closer to seven, after 33 goals last season.

We'd stay calm. Colorado gets 56% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with Nelson on at five on five, better than without him, and Evolving-Hockey had him in the 98th percentile last season for driving offense once teammates are accounted for, with a note that he was better than his goals then too. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the home-plate area in front of the net as well as almost anyone. At 35, decline is always the worry, but his top speed still ranks in the league's top tenth. Our projection's middle case is 23 more goals; the chances say the slow stretch is a blip.
headline: Slow start, steady process
